basis_statement: Exact decimals stay canonical string literals at contract and persistence boundaries while runtime helpers preserve unscaled integer precision plus explicit scale.

source_lineage.source_heading_or_logical_block: exact decimal and money scale rules
source_lineage.rationale: Money and trust formulas require exact decimal strings with fixed scale and no float coercion.
Replay-safe serialization depends on exact decimal string fidelity.
Validator behavior is the executable guardrail for no-exponent, no-locale, no-negative-zero decimal parsing.

forbidden_inputs.label: Negative zero is illegal
forbidden_inputs.reason: The validator explicitly rejects negative-zero serialization.

forbidden_inputs.label: Exponent notation is forbidden
forbidden_inputs.reason: Canonical decimal strings may not use exponent form.

forbidden_inputs.label: Locale separators are forbidden
forbidden_inputs.reason: Locale formatting would make replay and hashing non-deterministic.

forbidden_inputs.label: Lossy number input is forbidden
forbidden_inputs.reason: The shared layer parses canonical string literals only.

operation_examples.label: Addition uses the maximum operand scale by default
Explicit scale keeps fixed money shape

comparison_examples.label: Different scales can be numerically equal but representationally distinct
